content: 1. Indication-Specific Dosing for Rose Hips (Rosa canina): To prepare rose hip tea, use 5 grams of crushed rose hips steeped in 150 mL of boiling water for 10–15 minutes. Strain the liquid before consumption. There are no established limits on the daily consumption of rose hip tea. 2. Nutritional and Therapeutic Benefits of Rose Hips: Rose hips are a rich source of Vitamin C, containing approximately 1700–2000 mg per 100 grams of dried product. They are used as a remedy for rheumatoid arthritis and to alleviate symptoms of knee and hip osteoarthritis. Rose hips support the immune system in combating foreign pathogens and abnormal cell growth. They facilitate fat metabolism and protect tissues from free radical damage. They assist the nervous system by converting specific amino acids into neurotransmitters. Rose hips prevent scurvy, protect joints and connective tissues, and support adrenal function. They may help prevent urinary bladder infections and alleviate dizziness and headaches. When used externally in oil form, rose hips restore skin firmness by nourishing and astringing tissues. When brewed into a decoction, rose hips can be used to treat constipation. Due to their high iron content, rose hip tea is often consumed during menstruation to compensate for iron loss. 3. Drug Interactions with Rose Hips: Tetracyclines (e.g., demeclocycline, doxycycline, minocycline, oxytetracycline, tetracycline): Rose hips reduce the absorption of these drugs in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. Eltrombopag: Rose hips decrease its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction is contraindicated. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. Fluoroquinolones (e.g., fleroxacin, gemifloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, ofloxacin): Rose hips reduce the absorption of these drugs in the GI tract. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. Levothyroxine and Liothyronine: Rose hips reduce their absorption in the GI tract. Use caution and monitor. Mycophenolate: Rose hips decrease its absorption in the GI tract. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. Iron Supplements: Rose hips interact with oral iron administration, potentially altering absorption. Use caution and monitor. Proton Pump Inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole, esomeprazole, lansoprazole, pantoprazole, rabeprazole): These drugs reduce the effect of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. H2-Receptor Antagonists (e.g., cimetidine, famotidine, nizatidine): These drugs reduce the effect of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. Calcium Salts (e.g., calcium carbonate, calcium citrate, calcium acetate): These reduce the absorption of rose hips in the GI tract. Conversely, rose hips may enhance the absorption of calcium salts. Use caution and monitor. Aspirin and Aspirin Combinations (e.g., aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate): Rose hips may increase the levels of aspirin by competing for renal tubular clearance. Aspirin may also reduce the levels of rose hips by increasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor. Methotrexate: Rose hips may increase its levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. Amoxicillin, Ampicillin, and Other Penicillins (e.g., penicillin G, penicillin VK): Rose hips may alter renal clearance, affecting drug levels. Use caution and monitor. Deferoxamine: Ascorbic acid in rose hips increases the availability of iron for chelation with deferoxamine. Avoid in patients with cardiac failure undergoing deferoxamine therapy. Clinical cardiac monitoring is recommended. Ibuprofen/Famotidine Combination: This combination reduces the effect of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. Sodium Bicarbonate and Sodium Citrate: These reduce the effect of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor. Acidic Drugs (e.g., acyclovir, aspirin, methotrexate): Rose hips may increase their levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. Barbiturates (e.g., amobarbital, butabarbital, butalbital): These drugs increase the elimination of rose hips, reducing their levels. Use caution and monitor. Cephalosporins (e.g., cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir): Rose hips may increase their levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 4. Pregnancy and Lactation Considerations: There is limited data on the safety of rose hips during pregnancy and lactation. Use caution and consult a healthcare provider before use. 5. Cost Information: The cost of rose hips and related products may vary depending on the form (e.g., tea, oil, supplements) and region.
